title: multi-region-dr-reserve-capacity-plan-q2-2026
content:
Multi-region DR Reserve & Failover Capacity Planning (GPU Fleet) - Q2 2026

This sheet captures current fleet inventory, utilization, and computed spare/failover reserves across regions. Focus: ensure multi-region redundancy and defined DR reserve for single-region failure and zonal outages. Assumptions:
- Target RTO for regional failover: 10 minutes for API endpoints; 30 minutes for batch workloads.
- Target RPO: 1 minute for cached state; "cold" tasks can accept up to 15 minutes of state reconsolidation.
- Warm spare = already booted instances with model cache primed; Cold spare = unprovisioned capacity that can be brought up within configured scaling windows.
- Safety margin: maintain min(absolute 50 GPUs, 15% of region running fleet) as cross-region DR reserve.

CSV TABLE HEADERS:
Region,Zone,GPU Type,Total GPUs,Prod Reserved (INST),Observed 95th Util (%),Average Daily Token Throughput,Peak QPS,Warm Spare (INST),Cold Spare (INST),Failover Reserve Requirement (INST),DR Reserve Target (INST),Notes

Rows:
us-west1,us-west1-a,A100-80GB,320,260,87,1.2e9,1,200,24,36,80,120,Priority west-coast traffic; warm spare placed in same region for zonal failover
us-east1,us-east1-b,A100-80GB,400,300,79,1.6e9,1,500,30,70,100,150,Primary east-coast capacity; cross-region failover plan points to us-west1 and eu-west1
eu-west1,eu-west1-b,A100-80GB,240,180,82,900e6,900,18,42,60,90,EU compliance-sensitive; DR reserve partially isolated
ap-southeast1,ap-southeast1-a,A40-48GB,160,110,74,420e6,350,12,38,40,60,Lower baseline; DR reserve leveraged only for APAC burst black swan events

Computed totals and policy lines:
Total Fleet GPUs (all regions): 1120
Total Prod Reserved Instances: 850
Weighted average observed 95th util: 81%
Target warm spare percent (policy): 5% per region (min 12 GPUs)
Target cold spare percent (policy): 10% per region (or min 24 GPUs)
Cross-region DR reserve policy: maintain at least 15% of global prod reserved GPUs (>=127 INST) distributed such that losing any single region still preserves 80% of baseline throughput via warm/cold reallocation and traffic routing.

Failover sizing examples (calculation notes):
- us-west1 failover requirement: if us-west1 (260 prod INST) fails, we need to absorb ~260 INST across us-east1 + eu-west1 + ap-southeast1. Current immediate warm capacity across peers = (30 + 18 + 12) = 60 INST. Cold capacity on-demand = (70 + 42 + 38) = 150 INST. Total absorbable = 210 INST -> shortfall 50 INST. DR Reserve Target for global buffer recommends adding 50 INST to cold reserve pool or reassigning 50 INST from scheduled non-critical workloads.
- eu-west1 failover requirement: 180 INST -> peers warm+cold absorb = (24+30+12)+(36+70+38)=.. modeled similarly -> recommended DR buffer 30 INST allocated in eu-west1 adjacent regions for compliance-safe handling.

Operational SLAs and actions:
1) Maintain warm spares distribution: at least 50% of warm spare capacity must be in-region (zonal diversification) to handle zone-level failures without cross-region egress.
2) Cold reserve automation: Terraform + Autoscaler templates to allow spin-up of cold reserve with pre-provisioned images and model cache hooks; target cold instance boot time <= 7 minutes.
3) Network readiness: pre-warmed LB endpoints in each region with failover routing rules. BGP health checks + Traffic Manager runbooks.
4) Cost control: cold reserve should be tagged and billed to "DR-Reserve" project code to track monthly $/GPU-hour impact.

Cost estimate (monthly, rough):
- Warm spare incremental cost: 5% of fleet active -> ~55 INST * $10k/GPU-month -> $550k/month (example A100-80GB premium)
- Cold reserve incremental cost: 10% fleet -> 110 INST * $3k/GPU-month (spot/preemptible mix) -> $330k/month
- Total rough DR incremental: ~$880k/month before optimizations (commit discounts, reserved pricing).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: cold boot time > RTO -> Mitigate with more warm spares or faster images + model snapshots in NVMe.
- Risk: cross-region egress costs during failover -> Mitigate via regional model pinning, degrade to smaller model variants automatically.
- Risk: capacity fragmentation -> Introduce quarterly defragmentation (rebalancing) windows with brief traffic shaping.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- [Asha] finalize warm/cold thresholds per region and submit to SRE policy board (ETA 2026-03-20)
- [Michael] implement autoscaler templates for cold reserve boot sequence and test with canary failover (ETA 2026-04-05)
- [Ruth] prepare RBAC + billing labels for DR-Reserve project and cost dashboards (ETA 2026-03-30)
- [Leo] run two tabletop DR exercises covering: single-region outage (us-east1) and zonal outage (us-west1-a) and capture RTO/RPO deviations (ETA 2026-04-12)

Revision history:
- 2026-02-18 initial draft created (Asha)
- 2026-02-25 added computed failover shortfall numbers after capacity audit (Michael)
- 2026-03-10 updated warm/cold policy and cost estimates; moved status to in_review (Asha)

Notes to reviewers:
- Please comment on warm vs cold percentage tradeoffs and any region-specific constraints (compliance or partner-hosted racks).
- If we accept increased warm spares for EU due to compliance, recommend offsetting with deeper spot usage in APAC to keep cost neutral.
